transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, well, I guess what made me bring it up is that... well, after some really long days on the construction site—I'm a supervisor, so I'm constantly putting out fires, you know? Like just last week, we had this massive issue with the drywall delivery, they brought the wrong thickness and the whole schedule got pushed back, which meant I had to stay late and deal with the contractor who was already in a terrible mood. Anyway, after days like that, or sometimes after these neighborhood association meetings I go to—which are a whole other headache, honestly, Mrs. Higgins will not let the landscaping issue go—I'll come home and just... eat way more than I ever meant to. Like, I'll go through leftover takeout, half a box of cereal, bags of chips, just whatever is sitting there, until I'm so uncomfortably full. My kitchen is usually pretty stocked because I try to meal prep on Sundays, but then I just kind of lose track of what I'm doing.
After these episodes where you feel like you've eaten too much, do you ever make yourself sick, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to try to compensate or make up for it?

Um, yeah... I mean, maybe a few times a month, if it's been a really bad night, I'll go into the bathroom and make myself throw up. I just panic, you know? I panic about undoing all the work I've put into looking put-together. It’s so important in my industry. Being a female supervisor on a site, you have to look sharp and authoritative, otherwise the guys just don't respect you. 

Like, I spend good money on these tailored work pants from this brand I found online—they're heavy canvas but they fit almost like nice slacks?—because if I show up looking even a little soft or sloppy, the electricians will walk all over me. Especially Gary. Oh my gosh, Gary is the absolute worst. He always tries to talk over me during the morning safety briefings. Just yesterday he tried to tell me the wiring for the second-floor HVAC was up to code when I could clearly see the conduit was completely exposed. I had to pull the blueprints out right there on the hood of my truck to prove him wrong. 

But anyway, my bathroom... actually, I just retiled my master bathroom myself last month. Classic subway tile with charcoal grout. It looks amazing, but the grout was an absolute nightmare to seal. I spent an entire Saturday on my knees scrubbing it. Wait, I'm sorry, what exactly did you ask me again?
During these times when you're eating a lot, do you feel like you're losing control—like you can't stop eating or can't control what or how much you're eating?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Once I start on those evenings, it really feels like I’m just on autopilot. Like, I’ll be actively telling myself in my head to stop because I have an early crew start the next morning, but I just keep going back to the kitchen for more anyway. 

And honestly, those early starts are brutal. My alarm goes off at 4:15 AM, and if I'm not on site by 5:30, the concrete guys just stand around waiting for someone to hold their hand. Plus, the coffee maker in the site trailer has been broken for three weeks. I put in a requisition for a new one, but Susan in purchasing is dragging her feet. She actually claims she needs three separate vendor quotes for a sixty-dollar machine! It's absurd. So I've been having to stop at this drive-thru place, which adds twenty minutes to my commute, and their lids never stay on tight. I spilled a whole Americano down the cup holder of my truck on Tuesday and it is impossible to get the sticky residue out of those little plastic crevices. I tried using a detailing brush, but it just smeared it around. 

Um, but yeah, sorry. When I'm in the kitchen at night, I just can't seem to make myself stop, no matter what I tell myself.
Do these episodes of overeating and feeling out of control cause you a lot of distress, or interfere with your work, relationships, or other areas of your life?

Um, well, it's definitely stressful. Like, I'm still showing up every day and doing my job, but... I don't know, it's starting to mess with my schedule a bit. Like, I've been turning down some of the after-meeting food plans with the neighborhood association. Which honestly might be a blessing in disguise because if I have to sit through another dinner listening to Mrs. Higgins complain about the height of the Johnson's new privacy fence, I might actually lose my mind. I swear, that woman has a measuring tape in her purse. She actually went over there on a Sunday afternoon to measure the pickets! 

But, yeah, I just... I rush home instead because I'm so worried the evening will get away from me and I'll end up in the kitchen again. And rushing home in this city's traffic is its own kind of nightmare. The construction on I-95 has been going on for, what, three years now? They just closed the left lane near my exit, and the detour they set up makes absolutely no sense. It loops you through this residential neighborhood with speed bumps every hundred feet. My truck suspension is practically shot as it is from hauling materials. I need to take it in to get the shocks looked at, but finding a reliable mechanic who doesn't try to talk down to me because I'm a woman is exhausting. The last guy tried to tell me I needed premium blinker fluid. I mean, can you believe that? I laughed right in his face. 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the distress. Yeah, it just... it makes me anxious, you know? Just worrying about how the night is going to go.
Do these episodes of eating a lot usually happen in response to emotional stress, like feeling upset, anxious, or overwhelmed, rather than just being tired or having a long day?

Um, well, I guess... I'm not really sure if it's always stress, exactly? I mean, my job is stressful, obviously, but sometimes it just happens when I finally sit down after a long day. But speaking of feeling overwhelmed, you wouldn't believe the stress I'm under with this new supplier we're using for lumber. 

I mean, the regional manager, Dave, assured me they could handle the volume for the new townhouse project, but their first delivery was short by three pallets of two-by-fours. Three pallets! And they didn't even call to tell me. I had a whole framing crew standing around at 7 AM with nothing to do. Do you know how much it costs to pay six union carpenters to lean on their hammers and complain about the weather? It's astronomical. And when I called Dave, he had the nerve to tell me the truck broke down. Like, I run a fleet of trucks, Dave, I know what a breakdown looks like, and I also know you can rent a flatbed if you really care about your clients. 

I ended up having to drive to three different big-box hardware stores myself, just loading up the back of my truck with whatever premium grade they had left on the racks, just to keep the guys moving. My lower back is still killing me from hauling it all. I really need to start going back to that chiropractor on 4th Street, but her receptionist is always so rude when I try to book an evening appointment. 

But, um, I guess I haven't really noticed a specific pattern with the eating being tied to stress. It just sort of... happens. Wait, did you mean stress from work, or just in general?
How often do these episodes where you feel out of control while eating happen—like, how many times a week or month?

Um, looking back over the last few months, I'd say the whole pattern—you know, the overeating and then purging afterwards—it averages out to about once a week. I mean, it really fluctuates. Some weeks it happens twice, and other weeks it doesn't happen at all. 

Like last week was a zero week because I was just completely dead on my feet. We had this massive drywall delivery for the second floor of that townhouse project, and of course, the freight hoist failed. Just completely died on Tuesday morning. The elevator tech the rental company sent out looked like he was about twelve years old, I swear. He spent three hours staring at the control panel while watching YouTube tutorials on his phone! I'm not even kidding. I had to pull my guys off framing to manually carry three hundred sheets of drywall up a temporary stairwell. By the time I got home those nights, my arms felt like wet noodles. I didn't even have the energy to open the fridge, let alone do anything else. I actually tried to use my massage gun on my shoulders, but the battery was dead because my dog, Buster—he's a golden retriever mix, total menace—chewed right through the charging cable. I had to wrap the pieces in electrical tape just to throw them in the trash so he wouldn't try to swallow the copper wire. He ate a whole work glove once and it cost me two grand at the emergency vet. 

Wait, sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, how often it happens. Yeah, so it really just depends on what's going on, but probably once a week on average.
